title: One loop tick
lede: What the orchestrator does each time its loop wakes: handle finished work, reconcile, fill free slots, and make sure work is moving.

wake.name: Wake
wake.role: A native /loop or an external driver fires the tick.
details: Timers are only for external gating, a usage-limit window or a crash re-arm.
risks: A timer is never used to pace the agent's own work; that work runs continuously.

topology.name: Read topology
topology.role: The orchestrator reads which worker slots exist from topology.json.
details: An invalid file is a blocker to report. No file means the orchestrator works alone.

review.name: Finished slots
review.role: Review each finished slot's work, integrate or ship it, and set the task status.
details: Integration and shipping stay within existing authorization.
Status becomes done, fail, or park --resume.

reconcile.name: Reconcile
reconcile.role: Make active tasks match live subagents and resolve leftover worktrees.

details.t: Compare live handles, active tasks and the git worktree list
more: Task with no subagent: resume or park.
Zombie worktree: integrate, park or clean.
Orphan owner: adopt into a slot or park.

dispatch.name: Free slots
dispatch.role: Give each free slot the highest-priority task it suits, in a new worktree.
details: A slot is free when no active task is owned by its id.
Order: create the worktree, claim the task for the slot, then start the slot's harness and model there.
No suited task? Leave the slot free.

supervise.name: Supervise
supervise.role: Check that each job advanced since the last tick, not just that it is running.
details: Check the leaf step, orphans, and who holds a shared budget.
A probe exits non-zero on an anomaly, which starts an investigation.
risks: A running process is not proof that work is moving.
qs: How does the orchestrator tell a stuck subagent from a slow one?

slot.d: A worker seat (a model plus a tool) that the orchestrator hands tasks to; its id names the task owner.

harness.d: The agent tool a slot runs, such as claude, codex, agy or pi.

zombie.d: A worktree an interrupted session left behind.

park.d: Return a task to pending, keeping its branch and a resume note.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand what scaffold's orchestrator does on each tick of its autonomous loop.
